question: What is the main cause of chest pain in angina pectoris?

options.A: Permanent damage to heart tissue from blocked vessels
options.B: Inflammation of the sac around the heart
options.C: Heart muscle lacking enough oxygen because supply cannot meet demand
options.D: An electrical problem in the heart's natural pacemaker

explanation: Angina happens when the heart muscle demands more oxygen than the narrowed coronary arteries can deliver. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which factor makes the heart muscle need more oxygen during exercise?

options.B: Lower fluid volume before heart contraction
options.D: Reduced squeezing strength of the heart

explanation: A faster heart rate increases the metabolic workload of the myocardium and shortens diastolic filling time. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h1)

question: How do nitrate medications quickly relieve chest pain?

options.A: By blocking beta receptors in the heart
options.B: By widening veins to reduce the volume of blood returning to the heart
options.C: By raising blood pressure and blood vessel resistance
options.D: By speeding up the electrical signals in the heart

explanation: Nitrates relax venous smooth muscle, pooling blood in the body and lowering the volume of blood returning to the heart. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why do patients using nitrate skin patches need a daily patch-free break?

options.A: To lower the risk of high blood pressure
options.B: To stop the body from getting used to the drug and losing its effect
options.C: To give the coronary arteries time to squeeze tightly
options.D: To let the liver clear out waste products

explanation: Continuous 24-hour exposure to nitrates depletes sulfhydryl groups, rendering the drugs ineffective unless a daily rest period is enforced. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the main way beta-blockers help manage angina?

options.A: By stopping blood clots from forming
options.B: By slowing the heart rate and reducing the force of its contractions
options.C: By relaxing veins to reduce blood returning to the heart
options.D: By blocking calcium from entering muscle cells

explanation: Beta-blockers block sympathetic stimulation on the heart, lowering heart rate and force of contraction to reduce oxygen demand. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h3)

question: What dangerous heart problem can happen if a patient suddenly stops taking a beta-blocker?

options.A: Dangerously high blood pressure and severe return of chest pain
options.B: Sudden fluid buildup in the lungs
options.C: Extreme low blood pressure from open blood vessels
options.D: A permanent heart block needing an emergency pacemaker

explanation: Sudden withdrawal causes beta-receptor upregulation, leaving the heart hypersensitive to circulating adrenaline. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h3)

question: How do calcium channel blockers work in the body?

options.A: By stopping the kidneys from reabsorbing calcium
options.B: By stopping calcium from entering blood vessel and heart muscle cells
options.C: By binding directly to calcium in the bloodstream to clear it
options.D: By releasing stored calcium quickly inside muscle fibers

explanation: Blocking calcium channels prevents the ion from entering muscle cells, which stops the contraction process and induces relaxation. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which specific type of angina responds best to calcium channel blockers?

options.A: Unstable angina caused by plaque tearing
options.C: Stable angina brought on only by heavy exercise
options.D: Chest pain that does not respond to any medicine at all

explanation: Calcium channel blockers directly relax coronary smooth muscle, making them ideal for preventing and treating sudden coronary spasms. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h4)

question: How does the drug ranolazine work differently to treat angina?

options.A: By blocking beta receptors directly on the heart
options.B: By raising overall blood vessel tone
options.C: By blocking late sodium currents inside heart muscle cells
options.D: By widening blood vessels far away from the heart

explanation: Ranolazine decreases intracellular sodium and subsequent calcium overload, improving myocardial efficiency without changing heart rate. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h5)

question: What makes ivabradine different from standard beta-blockers?

options.A: It widens veins while making heart contractions stronger
options.B: It blocks calcium channels only in blood vessel walls
options.C: It prevents blood platelets from sticking together in narrowed arteries
options.D: It lowers the heart rate without causing major changes in blood pressure

explanation: Ivabradine targets the SA node directly through funny channels, reducing heart rate without the negative inotropic or hypotensive effects of beta-blockers. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which vital signs must a nurse check before giving a beta-blocker?

options.A: Blood electrolyte and kidney function levels
options.D: Skin color and how fast color returns when pressed

explanation: Because beta-blockers lower both heart rate and blood pressure, checking these parameters first prevents dangerous hypotension and bradycardia. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which common side effect of certain calcium channel blockers is often mistaken for heart failure?

options.A: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: Selective arteriolar dilation causes fluid to shift into the interstitial spaces of the lower extremities, creating dependent edema. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is an important rule for storing sublingual nitroglycerin tablets?

options.A: Keep them out in the open air on a small ceramic dish
options.B: Keep them in the refrigerator at all times
options.C: Store them in a clear plastic bag in the bathroom
options.D: Keep them in their original dark, airtight glass bottle

explanation: Nitroglycerin loses its potency when exposed to light, moisture, and heat, requiring specialized dark glass packaging. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why should patients never take nitrates and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (like sildenafil) together?

options.A: It stops the liver from breaking down either drug
options.B: It causes an immediate and permanent spasm of the heart arteries
options.C: It completely cancels out the heart benefits of the nitrate
options.D: It causes a dangerous, life-threatening drop in blood pressure

explanation: Both classes of drugs cause profound vasodilation through cyclic GMP pathways, and combining them results in catastrophic hypotension. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h7)
